questions.q: Traditionally, which kata is taught FIRST?
options: Taikyoku Shodan
Heian Godan
Bassai Dai
Kanku Dai
questions.explanation: Taikyoku Shodan (First Cause) is simplest embusen. Then Heian Shodan. Heian = peaceful mind.

questions.q: A new student joins. Before any punch, what should they learn FIRST besides technique?
options: Dojo etiquette, safety, how to fall, Rei
How to break boards
Tournament rules
Advanced kata
questions.explanation: Etiquette before technique - the traditional first lesson: Rei, lining up, tying the belt, safe distance.

questions.q: Bunkai means:
options: Application / analysis of kata movements
Board breaking
Meditation
Belt test
questions.explanation: Bunkai = to take apart. Each kata move has grappling, striking, throwing applications hidden inside.

questions.q: Kokutsu Dachi is:
options: Back stance - 70% weight on back leg
Front stance
Sumo stance
One-leg stance
questions.explanation: Ko = back. Weight back, ready to defend and counter. Used in Heian Shodan.

questions.q: Heian means peaceful ____
options: Mind
Body
Fist
Way
questions.explanation: Heian = peaceful mind. Kata designed to develop calm under pressure.

questions.q: Wearing rings, earrings or chains during training is:
options: Forbidden - they can cut you and your training partners
Fine if they are small
Allowed if taped
Allowed for grading only
questions.explanation: Jewellery causes cuts and snags in kumite. A clean, bare, tidy appearance is part of dojo hygiene and respect.

questions.q: Sanbon Kumite means:
options: Three-step sparring - attacker does 3 attacks
Three person fight
30 minute sparring
Free fight
questions.explanation: San = three, hon = step. Pre-arranged 3 attacks to learn distance and timing.

questions.q: Where did Karate originally develop?
options: Okinawa - the Ryukyu Islands, blending native Te with Chinese fighting arts
Mainland Japan
Korea
China only
questions.explanation: Karate grew on Okinawa from native Te plus Chinese Quanfa, then travelled to mainland Japan in the early 1900s.

questions.q: 'Karate ni sente nashi' teaches that:
options: There is no first attack in karate
You should always strike first
Attacking wins tournaments
Kumite has no rules
questions.explanation: One of Funakoshi's Twenty Precepts: karate is for character and protection - never for starting violence.

questions.q: The word 'Osu' (Oss!) spoken in the dojo carries the meaning of:
options: Perseverance, endurance and respect
Just a greeting
Time to rest
Belt promotion
questions.explanation: From Oshi Shinobu - to push and endure. Osu compresses patience, respect and fighting spirit into one word.

questions.q: In traditional dojo culture, the Sempai-Kohai relationship means:
options: Senior students guide, support and set an example for juniors
Juniors command seniors
Seniors never speak to juniors
Everyone trains alone
questions.explanation: Sempai (senior) models etiquette and mentors; Kohai (junior) observes and learns. This living chain passes tradition down.

questions.q: Shu Ha Ri describes:
options: Stages of learning: obey form, break form, make form
Three katas
Three belts
Bowing types
questions.explanation: Shu (protect form), Ha (break from form), Ri (transcend). Student → innovator → master.

questions.q: Mokuso - the quiet meditation at the start and end of class - is for:
options: Calming the mind and leaving the outside world at the door
Catching your breath only
Checking your belt knot
Talking to friends
questions.explanation: Mokuso builds mushin - the clear mind. Tradition begins and ends training with stillness and gratitude.

questions.q: Dojo Kun #1: Hitotsu, Jinkaku Kansei ni Tsutomeru Koto - Means?
options: Seek perfection of character
Seek profit
Seek trophies
Seek revenge
questions.explanation: Perfection of character is first. Not perfect technique. Character.

questions.q: What does 'Karate-Do' literally translate to?
options: Way of the empty hand, a path
Way of the warrior in battle
School of hard fist fighting
Fist of fury way of power
questions.explanation: Kara = empty, Te = hand, Do = way/path. No weapons - just character development through empty-hand training.

questions.q: The Dojo Kun are five principles recited in the dojo. What is their main purpose?
options: To help us memorize kata names
To guide us to build strong character first
To teach how to win tournaments
To learn counting in Japanese
questions.explanation: Seek perfection of character, be faithful, endeavor to excel, respect others, refrain from violent behavior. Dojo Kun puts character before technique.

questions.q: What does Rei mean and when do you perform it?
options: Bow of respect - when entering/leaving dojo and to partner
Attack command to start kumite
Forearm block against a punch
Only the final bow at a tournament
questions.explanation: Rei is respect made physical. You bow when entering/leaving dojo, to Sensei, Sempai and partner before/after kumite.

questions.q: In Kihon, what is Oi-Zuki?
options: Reverse punch from opposite side
Rising uppercut punch to chin
Elbow strike to close range
Lunge punch stepping forward with same side
questions.explanation: Oi = chasing/lunge. You drive forward with front leg and punch with same-side arm. First power punch every white belt learns.

questions.q: Karate training stands on three main pillars. What are they?
options: Stretching, shouting, and resting
Punching, kicking, and blocking only
Kihon, Kata and Kumite together
Kata, games, and grading events
questions.explanation: Kihon = fundamentals, Kata = forms, Kumite = sparring. These three pillars carry you from white belt to Judan.

questions.q: Zenkutsu Dachi - the first stance you learn - is described as:
options: Cat stance with most weight on back leg
Front stance with long, strong forward base
Straddle stance with knees wide apart
Hourglass stance with feet turned inward
questions.explanation: Zenkutsu = front stance. Front knee bent over toes, back leg straight, 60% weight front, 40% back. Root for Oi-Zuki and Gyaku-Zuki.

questions.q: Sensei says 'Yoi' and then 'Hajime' - what do they mean?
options: Bow and then sit in seiza
Prepare ready stance, then begin
Turn around and then stop
Line up and then bow deeply
questions.explanation: Yoi = get ready in Yoi Dachi, alert mind. Hajime = begin action. Yame = stop. These three run every kihon line.

questions.q: Count 1-5 correctly in Japanese dojo counting:
options: Ichi, Ni, San, Yon, Go
Ichi, Ni, San, Shi, Go
Uno, Dos, Tres, Cuatro, Cinco
One, Two, Three, Four, Five
questions.explanation: Ichi (1), Ni (2), San (3), Shi (4), Go (5). Sensei counts like this for kihon. In dojo, Shi is used for 4 instead of Yon to keep rhythm.

questions.q: Zenkutsu Dachi is which stance?
options: Back stance with weight on rear leg
Cat stance with high narrow posture
Horse stance with wide low base
Front stance - long, strong forward
questions.explanation: Zenkutsu = front stance. 60% weight front, front knee bent over toes, back leg straight, hips forward. Power base for Oi-Zuki and Gyaku-Zuki.

questions.q: What is the real purpose of Kiai?
options: To scare opponent with loud noise
To focus breath, tighten core, commit spirit
To get extra points from judges
To show off and look tough
questions.explanation: Kiai unites breath, body and intent. It tenses core for protection, drives hara power, and shows total commitment - not just shouting.

questions.q: TRUE or FALSE: Removing shoes before stepping on dojo floor is optional if you're in a rush.
options: True - rush is an exception allowed
False - always remove shoes first
questions.explanation: False. Always remove shoes. It's hygiene, respect for dojo, and safety. First lesson before any technique is etiquette.

questions.q: Kihon means:
options: Free sparring against partner
Pre-arranged forms and patterns
Philosophy of empty hand
Fundamentals and basic foundation
questions.explanation: Kihon is basics. Kihon, Kata, Kumite are three pillars. Without strong kihon, kata is empty and kumite is sloppy.

questions.q: In karate, your body is divided into three target levels. Name them:
options: Head level, body level, leg level
Upper strike, middle strike, low kick
Jodan, Chudan and Gedan levels
Tsuki, Uchi and Keri attacks
questions.explanation: Jodan = upper (head/neck), Chudan = middle (chest/stomach), Gedan = lower (below belt). Every attack and block names its level.

questions.q: Why must fingernails and toenails be short and hands clean before training?
options: It looks more fashionable for grading
To grip the floor better for balance
No reason - it is only old tradition
To protect partners and maintain dojo hygiene
questions.explanation: Short nails and clean hands/feet prevent scratches, cuts and infection. Clean gi, no jewellery, washed hands, short nails - basic safety and respect for partners.

questions.q: What is Gedan Barai and what level does it cover?
options: Upper rising block that covers jodan level
Middle inside block that covers chudan
Lower sweeping block that covers gedan
Knife-hand block that covers all levels
questions.explanation: Gedan = lower level, Barai = sweep. Gedan Barai sweeps attacks aimed below belt to side. First block taught with Zenkutsu Dachi.

questions.q: Traditionally, which kata is taught FIRST to beginners?
options: Heian Shodan
Heian Godan
Kanku Dai
Taikyoku Shodan
questions.explanation: Taikyoku Shodan (First Cause) has simplest embusen - only gedan barai and oi-zuki. Then Heian Shodan. Heian = peaceful mind.

questions.q: Kiba Dachi is also called horse stance. How do you stand?
options: Long front stance like Zenkutsu forward
Back stance with weight shifted to rear
Straddle stance with feet wide, knees bent outward
Cat stance with 90% weight on back foot
questions.explanation: Kiba = horse. Feet double shoulder width, toes slightly in, knees bent outward pushing knees open, back straight, like riding horse. Builds leg strength.

questions.q: Which Dojo Kun line says 'I shall guard against impertious courage' in Japanese?
options: Hitotsu, jinkaku kansei ni tsutomuru koto
Hitotsu, kekki no yu wo imashimuru koto
Hitotsu, doryoku no seishin wo yashinau koto
Hitotsu, reigi wo omonzuru koto
questions.explanation: Kekki no yu = violent courage/impulsive bravery. Line 5: Hitotsu, kekki no yu wo imashimuru koto - refrain from violent behavior, use restraint.

questions.q: Where does Gyaku-Zuki power REALLY start?
options: Floor reaction through legs, hip rotation, core, then fist
Shoulder muscle pushing arm forward alone
Big arm muscle flexing to punch hard
Quick wrist flick at the very end
questions.explanation: Power is ground reaction force. Push floor, drive legs, rotate hips, whip core, fist is just delivery. Not arm punching.

questions.q: Shuto Uke is:
options: Knife-hand block
Upper rising block with forearm
Lower sweeping block to gedan
Palm heel strike to the chin
questions.explanation: Shuto = knife-hand. Using the outside edge of the hand from little finger to wrist. Shuto Uke deflects jodan/chudan attacks in Kokutsu Dachi, then counters with shuto strike.

questions.q: What is the signature new technique introduced in Heian Sandan?
options: Only oi-zuki and gedan barai repeated
Kiba dachi with tettsui and simultaneous blocks
High jump like Kanku Dai
Only kokutsu dachi stance
questions.explanation: Heian Sandan introduces Kiba Dachi, tettsui (hammer fist), morote uke, and simultaneous gedan barai + uchi uke. First kiba stance kata.

questions.q: How is Shiko Dachi different from Kiba Dachi?
options: Same as kiba dachi - just different name
Toes turned out 45°, lower, sumo-like
One leg lifted like crane stance
Very narrow feet together stance
questions.explanation: Shiko = sumo stance. Like kiba but toes out 45 degrees, knees pushing out, lower. Builds inner thigh and rooted stability. Kiba toes more forward.

questions.q: Ritsurei and Zarei - when do you use each?
options: Both mean same - just bow any way
Ritsurei = standing bow Zarei = kneeling bow
Ritsurei = attack, Zarei = defend
Ritsurei = kick, Zarei = punch
questions.explanation: Ritsurei = standing bow (entering dojo, to sensei, to partner). Zarei = kneeling seiza bow (start/end class to shomen and sensei). Both show respect.

questions.q: Maai means:
options: Fighting spirit and loud kiai
Proper distance and timing between opponents
Type of tournament trophy
Color of belt ranking
questions.explanation: Maai = engagement distance. Too close you get jammed, too far you miss. Sanbon Kumite teaches maai, timing, and zanshin.

questions.q: In traditional dojo culture, the Sempai-Kohai relationship means:
options: Senior students guide, support and set an example for juniors
Senior command Junior and give orders to follow
Seniors never speak to juniors at all
Everyone trains completely alone always
questions.explanation: Sempai (senior) models etiquette and mentors; Kohai (junior) observes, respects and learns. This living chain passes tradition down without words.

questions.q: Shu Ha Ri describes:
options: Three different kata with same name
Three types of belts in Shotokan
Stages of learning: obey form, break form, make form
Three different ways of bowing deeply
questions.explanation: Shu (protect/obey form), Ha (break from form, question), Ri (transcend, make your own). Student → innovator → master.

questions.q: What is Kime in Shotokan technique?
options: Focus of power with total body at impact moment
Shouting loudly to intimidate opponent
Dancing movement to look beautiful
Resting between techniques to recover
questions.explanation: Kime = decision, focus. Whole body tenses for an instant at impact - muscles, breath, mind. Then relaxes again. Snap focus, not stiff.

questions.q: Heian Yondan's signature technique that is new for this level is:
options: Only oi-zuki repeated again
Shuto uke, kosa dachi and yoko geri keage
High jump like Kanku Dai does
Only zenkutsu dachi stance
questions.explanation: Heian Yondan introduces Shuto Uke in Kokutsu, Kosa Dachi (cross stance), Yoko Geri Keage (side snap kick), and hiza geri. More complex embusen.

questions.q: Why does every kata have an Embusen (floor pattern)?
options: Just for decoration to look nice
To train direction changes
To make grading harder on purpose
No reason - random walking around
questions.explanation: Embusen = performance line. Teaches awareness, balance and spatial awareness. It forces you to turn, shift weight, maintain zanshin in 4 directions, and finish at same start point.

questions.q: Go No Sen in kumite means:
options: Attack first before opponent moves
Defend then counter
Both attack at same time together
Run away from opponent quickly
questions.explanation: Go = after, Sen = initiative. Go No Sen = defensive initiative - block opponent's attack then counter. Most basic kumite strategy for purple belt.

questions.q: Zanshin after delivering a technique means:
options: Remaining awareness
Falling down to rest after kiai
Turning your back on opponent
Celebrating your point loudly
questions.explanation: Zan = remain, Shin = mind/heart. Stay aware, keep guard, expect counter. Real fight doesn't end at one punch.

questions.q: How many lines does the Dojo Kun have?
options: Five lines
Three lines for three pillars only
Ten lines for ten commandments
One line only - just bow
questions.explanation: Five lines: Seek perfection of character, be faithful, endeavor, respect others, refrain from violent behavior. Each starts with Hitotsu - first, one thing, as one mind.

questions.q: Bushido virtue 'Gi' means:
options: Rectitude and right decision even when hard
Just courage to fight without thinking
Love of money and profit always
Physical strength alone to win
questions.explanation: Gi is doing what's right even when hard, not convenient. Core of warrior code, foundation of all other virtues.

questions.q: Tekki Shodan was originally called:
options: Naihanchi - side-to-side iron horse form
Heian Shodan - peaceful mind first
Taikyoku - first cause for beginners
Empi - flying swallow kata
questions.explanation: Naihanchi = side-to-side. Kiba Dachi iron horse stance. Old Okinawan roots for close combat with back to wall, grappling and elbows.

questions.q: What is the difference between Ibuki and Nogare breathing?
options: Ibuki = hard power breathing, Nogare = soft calm breathing
Both are exactly the same breathing method
Only for black belts, not for brown belts
Not used at all in Shotokan training
questions.explanation: Ibuki = hard, audible, tension for power and kime. Nogare = soft, silent, calm for recovery and flow between techniques. Both train breath control.

questions.q: Gichin Funakoshi brought Karate from Okinawa to mainland Japan in 1922.
options: True - demonstrated in Tokyo and spread Karate-Do
False - Karate started in Tokyo originally
questions.explanation: True. 1922 demonstration in Tokyo. Father of modern Karate-Do. Wrote Karate-Do Kyohan and 20 Precepts. Changed Kara from Chinese hand to empty hand.

questions.q: What should brown belt grading test most?
options: Fancy high kicks that look impressive
Breaking five boards with one punch
Consistency under pressure - basics never failing when tired
Speed only, no need for accuracy
questions.explanation: Brown is refinement. Basics must be automatic even when exhausted, under pressure, with zanshin. Flashy without foundation fails.

questions.q: Bassai Dai translates to:
options: To storm a fortress - breaking through defense
Peaceful mind like Heian series
Flying swallow like Empi kata
Iron horse like Tekki Shodan
questions.explanation: Bassai = to storm fortress. Dai = big. Kata teaches breaking through opponent's strong defense with power, changing rhythm and hip drive.

questions.q: What is Sen No Sen in kumite?
options: Counter after opponent finishes attack completely
Attack at exact moment opponent starts to attack
Both fighters run away from each other
No initiative, just waiting forever
questions.explanation: Sen No Sen = initiative within initiative. Attack on opponent's intention/start. Higher than Go No Sen. Requires reading maai and intention.

questions.q: Funakoshi's Niju Kun (20 Precepts) - how many precepts are there?
options: Five precepts like Dojo Kun
Twenty precepts for daily life and training
Ten precepts only for tournaments
One precept - just work hard
questions.explanation: Niju Kun = 20 precepts. Karate begins and ends with courtesy, no first attack, karate is lifelong, etc. Dojo Kun is 5, Niju Kun is 20.

questions.q: What is Kake Waza (hooking technique) example?
options: Hooking block that pulls opponent off balance to counter
Straight punch with no hooking at all
High kick to head only
Bowing without technique
questions.explanation: Kake = hook. Kake Uke, Kake Geri. Hook opponent's arm/leg to break balance, create opening. Brown belt level kumite uses hooking, trapping.

questions.q: Empi means flying swallow and includes:
options: Only slow movements without jumps
Only Kiba Dachi stance
Jump, spinning, dropping to floor - swallow movements
Only punching without kicks
questions.explanation: Empi = flying swallow. Light, fast, jump, 360 turn, drop to floor. Swallow evades and strikes. Signature of Empi kata, shows agility.

questions.q: In WKF Kumite, what scores Yuko (1 point)?
options: Jodan kick or any scoring technique on fallen opponent
Chudan punch to body with good form, distance, timing
Sweep that drops opponent completely
Punch that misses target intentionally
questions.explanation: Yuko = 1 point: Chudan or Jodan Tsuki/Uchi. Waza-ari = 2 points (chudan kick). Ippon = 3 points (jodan kick or technique on fallen opponent). All need 6 criteria.

questions.q: Why must Dogi (gi) be clean, white, and properly tied for grading?
options: Just to look good for photos
Clean white gi shows respect
Any color is fine for grading
Dirty gi shows hard training only
questions.explanation: Dogi = way clothing. Discipline and readiness, Clean, white, no wrinkles, belt tied correctly shows discipline, respect for art, sensei and self. Mind and appearance connect.

questions.q: Best core training for karate power transfer?
options: Anti-rotation, bracing and breathing control for transfer
Six pack crunches only for looks
No core needed for karate technique
Fast situps until failure only
questions.explanation: Karate core is anti-movement and power transfer, not just flex. Planks, Pallof press, dead bug with breathing, bracing for kime. Not six pack.

questions.q: A well-managed traditional class always:
options: Opens and closes with formal rei, mokuso and set structure
Starts immediately with free sparring hard
Has no fixed plan, random each time
Ends whenever students feel like leaving
questions.explanation: Rei-in, warm-up, kihon, kata, kumite, cool down, rei-out. Predictable structure builds discipline, safety, respect, and learning progression.

questions.q: Before allowing kumite, the sensei managing the class must:
options: Inspect space, pair by size and grade, set contact level clearly
Leave students to fight freely without rules
Allow full contact for everyone regardless
Skip warm-up to save time
questions.explanation: Class management is prevention: safe space check, smart pairing (size/grade/experience), clear rules, contact level, mouthguards, control. Safety first.

questions.q: A senior student accidentally damages dojo equipment. The right response?
options: Repair it in secret without telling anyone
Hide damage and hope no one notices
Report immediately and help repair or replace it
Ignore it and leave dojo
questions.explanation: Dojo management runs on honesty and responsibility - same character karate builds on floor. Own mistake, report to sensei, fix. Sempai models integrity.

questions.q: Student offers extra money to grade early before time-in-grade. You as Sandan?
options: Explain standard, time in grade matters, integrity over fee
Grade anyway for money
Charge double and grade quickly
Ignore request completely
questions.explanation: Business ethics: belt integrity is dojo reputation. Short-term money kills long-term trust. Time in grade builds character and ensures standard.

questions.q: Meikyo means "Bright Mirror" - Sandan kata. What defines it?
options: Only horse stance with no jumps
Sankaku jump and mirror-like calm reflecting opponent
Beginner kata for white belts
Only punching without defense
questions.explanation: Meikyo = bright mirror. Sankaku tobi (triangle jump), calm mind reflecting like mirror. First move like holding mirror. Tests balance and clear mind.

questions.q: For Sandan teaching mawashi geri safely, what hip action prevents injury?
options: Hip locked, only knee twisting forcefully
Hip opens fully, support foot pivots 180°, knee tracks
No pivot needed, just kick high
Lean back excessively
questions.explanation: Hip opens, support foot pivots on ball, knee tracks over toes, hip and shoulder in line. Hip mobility plus core prevents knee injury.

questions.q: Gojushiho means 54 Steps. Difference between Dai and Sho for Sandan?
options: Dai = big, slow powerful; Sho = small, fast intricate - same origin
Same kata exactly
One is beginner, one advanced only
No difference
questions.explanation: Go = 5, Ju = 10, Shi = 4, Ho = steps. Dai = big - powerful, Sho = small - fast, intricate hand techniques. Both from same root, show yin/yang.

questions.q: What is Kizami Zuki used for in Sandan Jiyu Kumite?
options: Lead jab to control distance, probe and set up Gyaku Zuki
Only for kata without kumite use
Kick to head
Block only
questions.explanation: Kizami = jab with lead hand. Controls maai, breaks rhythm, measures distance, sets up gyaku, scores. Key for WKF style kumite.

questions.q: Fudoshin means:
options: Immovable mind - stable under pressure, not disturbed
Angry mind that attacks
Sleepy mind that rests
Confused mind
questions.explanation: Fu = not, Do = move, Shin = mind. Immovable mind like mountain, calm under pressure, not frozen but stable. Developed through hard training and mokuso.

questions.q: How should Sandan manage mixed level class (white to brown together)?
options: Teach same kata to all without adjustment
Layer instruction - same theme, different depth and tasks per grade
Only teach advanced kata
Only teach white belts
questions.explanation: Layered teaching: same theme (e.g., oi-zuki), white learns stance, green learns hip, brown learns timing and application. Everyone challenged, safety kept.

questions.q: Best breathing during kata for power and endurance?
options: Hold breath entire kata until dizzy
Breathe continuously with Nogare, exhale sharply with Ibuki on kime
Only breathe in, never out
Random breathing without pattern
questions.explanation: Continuous breathing - inhale Nogare (soft), exhale with technique, short Ibuki on kime. Never hold breath. Breath powers movement.

questions.q: What is JKA and its importance?
options: Japan Karate Association - founded 1949 by Funakoshi students to preserve Shotokan
Just a tournament name
A belt manufacturer
Only for Kyokushin
questions.explanation: JKA = Japan Karate Association, founded 1949 by Funakoshi and students like Nakayama. Standardized Shotokan, spread worldwide, produced first instructors.

questions.q: Chinte means "Strange Hands" - what is unique for Sandan?
options: Only normal blocks like others
Unusual hand techniques - double blocks, close finger strikes
Only kicks
Beginner kata
questions.explanation: Chin = strange/unusual, Te = hands. Rare techniques: double blocks, nippon nukite (two-finger), circular movements, close defense. Tests adaptability.

questions.q: As Sandan managing dojo business, best student retention strategy?
options: Only grade fast to keep them happy short term
Build community, clear progression, care, character over quick belts
Charge lowest price only
Never correct students
questions.explanation: Retention is not cheap belts. Community, friendships, clear goals, caring sempai-kohai, character development, fair standards keep students for years.

questions.q: Sandan sees kohai bullying at school. Per Dojo Kun, what is correct?
options: Encourage bullying to be tough
Teach that karate is for protection and character, intervene with compassion
Ignore as not dojo matter
Teach them to fight bully violently
questions.explanation: Dojo Kun extends outside dojo. Jinkaku kansei - seek perfection of character. Refrain from violent behavior, protect weak. Karate is for courage to do right.

questions.q: Uraken Uchi (backfist) power comes from:
options: Whip-like snap from elbow rotation and hip snap
Only arm muscle pushing
Shoulder only without body
Wrist only
questions.explanation: Uraken = backfist. Elbow snaps, forearm whips, hip snaps. Fast, close, surprise. Not push. Sandan must show snap vs push difference.

questions.q: Wankan means "King's Crown" - short kata for Sandan. What defines it?
options: Longest kata with 100 moves
Short 24 moves, one kiai, crown shape at start
Only horse stance
White belt kata
questions.explanation: Wan = king, Kan = crown. 24 moves, shortest advanced kata, one kiai only, crown shape with hands. Tests precision in short form.

questions.q: What changes at Yondan (4th Dan) level in traditional dojo?
options: You focus only on your own training now
You become steward of style - preserving and passing tradition
You stop training kihon completely
You only compete for trophies
questions.explanation: Yondan is not just stronger technique - it's stewardship. Preserve kata as taught, mentor black belts, protect dojo integrity for next generation.

questions.q: Kanku Sho vs Kanku Dai - what is Sho?
options: Same kata with different name only
Small version - faster, intricate, 47 moves vs 65, same origin
Beginner kata for white belts
Only horse stance
questions.explanation: Dai = big, Sho = small. Both view sky. Sho is small, fast, intricate, more jumps, tighter. Dai is big, powerful. Both required for Yondan.

questions.q: Difference between Kyu and Dan grades philosophically?
options: Kyu = learning technique, Dan = learning how to live technique
No difference at all
Kyu is higher than Dan
Dan means you stop learning
questions.explanation: Kyu = student grades (9-1) learning form. Dan = steps on the way - living karate, refining character, teaching. Shodan = beginning.

questions.q: What is Jiyu Ippon Kumite for Yondan level?
options: One attack, free movement, defender must choose defense spontaneously
Three step pre-arranged only
No rules brawl
Only kata
questions.explanation: Jiyu = free, Ippon = one. Attacker announces target (or not), free movement, one attack. Defender reads distance, blocks, counters freely. Bridge to Jiyu Kumite.

questions.q: Best feedback method for Yondan correcting Shodan's kata?
options: Only say "wrong" without why
One correction at a time, show why, let them feel, positive first
Correct 10 things at once loudly
Ignore mistakes
questions.explanation: Yondan teaching is precise - one key correction, explain why, demonstrate, let student feel difference, praise effort. Not overload.

questions.q: How should Yondan (often 40+) adapt training for longevity?
options: Same as 20 year old with no adaptation needed
More mobility, recovery, technique over brute force, smart load
Stop training completely
Only lift heavy weights
questions.explanation: Longevity: joint mobility, core, recovery, breathing, technique efficiency over muscle. Ibuki/Nogare, stretching, anti-rotation core, not just hard impact.

questions.q: Bassai Sho theme vs Bassai Dai?
options: Same as Dai exactly
Small fortress - more intricate, close defense, soft power
Beginner kata
Only kicks
questions.explanation: Bassai Dai = storm big fortress with power. Sho = storm small fortress - close, intricate, subtle, softer. Both teach breaking defense.

questions.q: As Yondan, how do you build strong dojo culture?
options: Rituals, shared language (Osu, Rei), sempai-kohai care, consistent standards
Only low fees
No etiquette needed
Allow disrespect
questions.explanation: Culture is built by rituals: rei in/out, mokuso, dojo kun recitation, clean dojo, sempai helping kohai, consistent standards, celebrating effort.

questions.q: Why "empty hand" still matters at Yondan with weapons everywhere?
options: It means no weapon in hand, but character is weapon - restraint and spirit
Means you have nothing
Outdated concept
Means you fight with empty hands only literally
questions.explanation: Kara = empty, but meaning deepens: empty of ego, anger, malice. Hand empty but spirit full. Karate is for protection and character, not violence.

questions.q: Jiin means "Temple Grounds" - Yondan kata. What defines it?
options: Only horse stance like Tekki
Slow start, broken rhythm, open hand defenses
Beginner kata
Only jumps
questions.explanation: Jiin = temple grounds. Similar to Jion/Jitte. Broken rhythm, slow to fast, open hands, guardian movements. Tests calm under irregular timing.

questions.q: What is Tai Sabaki for Yondan kumite?
options: Body shifting - moving off line, not just blocking hard
Only blocking with force
Running away
Standing still
questions.explanation: Tai = body, Sabaki = management. Move off attack line with ashi sabaki, evade and counter. Higher level than go no sen blocking.

questions.q: Yondan planning dojo succession - best practice?
options: Train 2-3 trusted Sandan/Nidan to teach same standard, document syllabus
Keep everything secret to yourself
Sell belt grades quickly
No plan needed
questions.explanation: Legacy: train successors, document kihon/kata/kumite curriculum, grading criteria, safety protocols. Dojo should outlive you.

questions.q: With Yondan power, ethical use outside dojo is:
options: Show off and intimidate others
Avoid conflict, de-escalate, protect weak, use karate last
Fight anyone who disrespects you
Use for profit only
questions.explanation: Higher grade = higher restraint. Power brings responsibility. Karate ni sente nashi, kekki no yu wo imashimuru - avoid violent behavior, protect.

questions.q: What is Kakushi Waza (hidden technique) in advanced kata?
options: Obvious block punch everyone sees
Hidden strike, sweep or lock inside apparent block
Only shouting
No hidden techniques exist
questions.explanation: Kakushi = hidden. Kata hides throws, locks, chokes inside blocks. Bassai Dai first move is not block - it's break and throw. Yondan must find hidden.

questions.q: Jitte means "Ten Hands" - Yondan kata. What does it teach?
options: Fighting against bo staff - using hands as ten, staff defense
Only white belt basics
Only kicking
Meditation only
questions.explanation: Jitte = ten hands. Originally defense against bo staff. Open hands, strong grips, staff defense movements. Power against weapon.

questions.topic: Philosophy • Shu Ha Ri at Yondan
questions.q: Where should Yondan be in Shu Ha Ri?
options: Still Shu - blindly obeying without question
Late Ha to early Ri - breaking form and making your understanding
Never reaching Ri
Ri means stop learning
questions.explanation: Shu (obey), Ha (break, question), Ri (transcend, create). Yondan is Ha to Ri - understands why form exists, adapts teaching, begins to express own karate while preserving root.

questions.q: Gankaku means "Crane on Rock" - Yondan kata. Signature?
options: Sagi ashi dachi - crane stance on one leg, balance and precision
Only horse stance
No balance needed
Beginner kata
questions.explanation: Formerly Chinto. Sagi ashi dachi (heron leg), crane stance, high kicks, balance on rock. Tests focus, balance, stillness like crane.

questions.q: Yondan on grading panel for Shodan - what fails a candidate even if kata looks good?
options: Poor rei, ego, unsafe control hurting partner, lack of dojo kun spirit
Only if they forget kata completely
Nothing fails, everyone passes
Only gi color
questions.explanation: Shodan is character grade. Poor etiquette, ego, unsafe kumite, disrespect to kohai, bad dojo kun understanding fails even if technique flashy. Character first.

questions.q: How do you teach Zanshin to brown belts as Yondan?
options: Tell them to drop guard after scoring
Drill - after technique, scan, keep guard, expect counter, breathe
No need to teach zanshin
Only shout zanshin word
questions.explanation: Teach by drill: after each combo, kiai, scan opponent, keep kamae, step back with guard. Zanshin is habit built through repetition and awareness.

questions.q: Student asks 'When will I be good enough?' Best answer as Nidan?
options: When you get black belt, you are good then
The path has no end - compare to yesterday only
Never - you will never be good enough at all
When you finally beat me in sparring today
questions.explanation: Do = way, not destination. Growth mindset, Shu Ha Ri is endless. Compare to yesterday's self, not others. Black belt is beginning, not end of path.

questions.q: First rule when a child is injured in class as instructor?
options: Tell them to walk it off quickly and continue
Stop, care, document, inform parent calmly now
Ignore injury and continue class as normal
Make them do pushups to toughen up fast
questions.explanation: Safety protocol + empathy + documentation = trust. Stop, assess, first aid, incident log, inform parent calmly, adjust training. Duty of care is first dan requirement.

questions.q: Unsu means "Cloud Hands" and is required for Nidan. What is its key theme?
options: Only slow walking with no jumps or spins at all
Cloud hands with 360 spin, jump and ippon drop
Only horse stance like Tekki Shodan always
Beginner kata with simple blocks only easy
questions.explanation: Un = cloud, Su = hands. Signature 360 spin on floor, jump with spinning shuto, ippon seoi nage motion. Symbolizes clouds gathering and dispersing. Tests agility and control.

questions.q: Jion kata is from Jion Temple. Its bunkai theme for Nidan is:
options: Only punching without any throws at all now
Defense against bo staff using temple guardian moves
Only high kicks for points in tournaments today
Just sitting meditation without movement now
questions.explanation: Jion = temple name. Rooted in Jionji temple. Contains juji uke (temple guardian), defense against bo staff, strong rooted stances. Bunkai shows temple guardian protecting.

questions.q: What is Sen No Sen vs Go No Sen for Nidan kumite?
options: Sen No Sen attacks on opponent's intention early
Go No Sen always means attack first quickly
Both mean running away from fight quickly
No difference between them at all really
questions.explanation: Go No Sen = after attack (defend then counter). Sen No Sen = during opponent's initiation - seize initiative. Sen Sen No Sen = before opponent even moves, reading intention. Higher level.

questions.q: As Nidan, how do you correct a green belt's Zenkutsu Dachi that is too high?
options: Just shout "lower" repeatedly without explanation
Explain knee over toes, hip forward, push floor well
Ignore mistake and hope it fixes itself later
Tell them to only do kata and skip kihon now
questions.explanation: Good teaching is not just telling what is wrong but why and how to feel it. Use tactile cue, analogy like pushing wall, show benefit. Shu Ha Ri teaching approach.

questions.q: Which 4 major styles came from Funakoshi's era students?
options: Shotokan, Shito-Ryu, Goju-Ryu, Wado-Ryu main styles
Only Shotokan exists in Japan today only
Karate has only one style ever in history
Kyokushin is the only style that exists now
questions.explanation: From Okinawa Te: Shotokan (Funakoshi), Shito-Ryu (Mabuni), Goju-Ryu (Miyagi), Wado-Ryu (Otsuka). All from early 20th century mainland spread.

questions.q: For Nidan teaching Kiba Dachi safely, what prevents knee injury?
options: Toes straight forward with knees caving inward badly
Toes slightly out, knees tracking over toes outward
Knees locked straight and stiff all the time now
Standing on toes only without heel support now
questions.explanation: Knee safety: toes slightly out 15-20 deg, knees push outward over toes, not caving in. Weight even, back straight. Builds strength not injury.

questions.q: "Do" in Karate-Do means:
options: Way or path of lifelong development beyond technique
Just a sport for tournaments only for medals
Only self-defense tricks for street fighting now
Dance performance for entertainment only now
questions.explanation: Do = way/path (like Judo, Kendo, Aikido). Not just jutsu (technique). Path of character, lifelong refinement. Nidan understands difference between jutsu and do.

questions.q: Sochin means "Tranquil Force" and is Nidan kata. What defines it?
options: Only fast movements without any power at all now
Fudo Dachi rooted stance with slow then explosive force
Only jumping kicks for tournament points now
White belt kata for beginners only easy now
questions.explanation: So = tranquil, Chin = force. Fudo Dachi (rooted/immovable stance), slow press then explosive. Strong, rooted, calm power like lion. Tests contrast of slow and fast.

questions.q: In WKF Kata competition, what are two main scoring areas?
options: Only speed matters for winning today in WKF
Technical and athletic performance plus bunkai demo
Only loud kiai shouting for points in WKF now
Gi color determines winner in WKF scoring now
questions.explanation: WKF scoring: Technical (70% - stances, techniques, embusen) and Athletic (30% - strength, speed, balance). Final bouts require bunkai demonstration of kata.

questions.q: What is Nidan's ethical duty outside dojo per Dojo Kun?
options: Show off to provoke fights outside dojo daily
Seek perfection of character, avoid violent behavior daily
Never help others outside dojo ever again now
Only care about belts and trophies always now
questions.explanation: Hitotsu, Jinkaku kansei ni... and Kekki no yu wo imashimuru. Nidan carries dojo reputation outside. Restraint, humility, helping society, not provoking.

questions.q: What is difference between Choku Zuki and Oi-Zuki/Gyaku-Zuki?
options: Choku Zuki is straight punch in place without step now
Same as Oi-Zuki exactly with no difference at all
Choku Zuki is a kick to head level only now
Choku Zuki is only for black belts advanced now
questions.explanation: Choku Zuki = straight punch in shizentai or kiba dachi, no step. Used to teach straight line, elbow, seiken. Foundation before moving punches.

questions.q: Nijushiho means 24 Steps and is for Nidan. What is unique?
options: Only 5 moves long and very short kata now
Flowing water-like rhythm with wall defense moves
Only horse stance without any other stance now
Beginner kata for white belts easy now only
questions.explanation: Nijushiho = 24 steps. Flowing, water-like, irregular rhythm, empi strikes, defense with back to wall. Tests fluid power and smooth transitions.

questions.q: Recite correct order of Dojo Kun 5 lines for Nidan test:
options: Character, Faithfulness, Endeavor, Etiquette, No violence
Winning, money, fame, power, ego always now
Only one line about bowing in dojo only now
Random order is fine for Nidan test always now
questions.explanation: 1 Seek perfection of character, 2 Be faithful, 3 Endeavor, 4 Respect others, 5 Refrain from violent behavior. Each starts with Hitotsu. Must recite by heart for Nidan.

questions.q: Mushin means:
options: No mind - clear mind without distraction, acting freely
Thinking too much about winning tournament now
Angry mind that attacks opponents always now
Sleepy mind that rests during class time now
questions.explanation: Mu = no/empty, Shin = mind. Not empty mind but clear mind, no fixation. Allows spontaneous correct action. Developed through mokuso and repeated kata.

questions.q: As Nidan on grading panel for kyu grades, what do you prioritize?
options: Consistency, etiquette, effort and safety over flashy tricks
Only who can break boards with power now only
Only tallest students in class always selected now
Only those who shout loudest in dojo always now
questions.explanation: Kyu grading is not tournament. Look for consistent kihon, good rei, effort, control, safety, spirit. Encourage growth, not perfection.

questions.q: Which describes Zanshin correctly for Shodan level?
options: Beginner belt that means white belt level
Loud shout to intimidate opponent only now
Fast kick to jodan level only for points now
Remaining mind with guard after technique done
questions.explanation: Zan = remain, Shin = mind. Zanshin is lingering awareness. After punch, you don't drop guard. You stay present, scan, ready for next. Essential for safety and real application.

questions.q: Adult beginner is frustrated because kids learn faster. As Shodan assistant instructor, what do you do?
options: Pair with patient sempai, focus on personal progress not comparison
Put adult in kids class to compete directly with children now
Tell adult to quit if they cannot keep up quickly now
Ignore frustration and push harder only without support
questions.explanation: Adult psychology: ego, comparison, time-poor, fear. Methodology must adapt - pair with supportive sempai, track personal progress, explain Shu Ha Ri stages.

questions.q: Who is recognized as founder of Shotokan and brought it from Okinawa to mainland Japan in 1922?
options: Mas Oyama who founded Kyokushin full contact style
Gichin Funakoshi, father of Shotokan karate-do
Chojun Miyagi who founded Goju-Ryu style system
Kenwa Mabuni who founded Shito-Ryu style system
questions.explanation: Gichin Funakoshi (1868-1957) father of Shotokan. Demonstrated at Ministry of Education exhibition in Tokyo 1922. Established Shotokan dojo, wrote Karate-Do Kyohan and 20 Precepts.

questions.q: In Dojo Kun, what does "Reigi o omonzuru koto" truly demand from a Shodan?
options: Perfecting technique before character development now
Seeking only victory in competition always for ego now
Respecting etiquette and manners above all in life
Avoiding physical conditioning completely as Shodan now
questions.explanation: Reigi o omonzuru koto = respect etiquette. For Shodan, technique without respect, humility and proper reigi is not true karate-do. Begins and ends with courtesy.

questions.q: What is significance of 26 Kata in Shotokan for 1st Dan examination?
options: Only 5 Heian are required for Shodan test level now
Kata is no longer required after black belt level now
Only freestyle kata is needed for Shodan test now
Shodan must know all 26 including Bassai Dai core kata
questions.explanation: Shodan must demonstrate mastery of full syllabus. Bassai Dai and Kanku Dai often mandatory for Shodan, representing bridge from Kihon to advanced principles of changing and viewing the sky.

questions.q: What is key biomechanical difference between Oi-zuki and Gyaku-zuki?
options: Both use identical hip movement exactly same always now
Gyaku-zuki is only used while retreating backward now
Oi-zuki is actually a kick not a punch at all now
Oi uses closed hanmi lunge, Gyaku uses full shomen rotation
questions.explanation: Oi-zuki drives forward same side arm/leg with hanmi. Gyaku-zuki anchors front leg and rotates hips fully to shomen to generate power from rear leg - core power technique.

questions.q: What does concept of "Kime" represent which every Shodan must demonstrate?
options: A loud kiai shout only for show without power now
Flexibility training for high kicks only for demo now
Total focus of body, mind, energy at impact moment
A type of free kumite tournament only for Shodan
questions.explanation: Kime = decision, focus. Total focus of body, mind, energy into single moment at end of technique. Instant focus of spirit, body contraction, breath, ki. Without kime, only movement.

questions.q: Kanku Dai means "To View The Sky" - what is its key theme for Shodan?
options: Only low stances without jumps or vision at all now
First kata for white belt beginners only easy now
Viewing sky with first move up, jump and 360 vision
Horse stance only without movement at all now
questions.explanation: Kan = view, Ku = sky. First move looks to sky, hands form triangle viewing sky. Includes manji uke, jump, 360 degree vision. 65 moves, most representative kata of Shotokan.

questions.q: Bassai Dai Bunkai for Shodan should show:
options: Only block and punch as seen externally simple now
Storming fortress - breaking grip, close combat, throwing
Only high kicks for tournament points now easy now
Meditation only without application at all now now
questions.explanation: Bassai = to storm fortress. Bunkai is not just block-punch. Entry breaking strong defense, grip breaks, close knee, throw, lock. Shodan must show application beyond omote.

questions.q: What does Maai and Hyoshi mean for Shodan Jiyu Kumite?
options: Just shouting louder than opponent always for win now
Control of distance, timing and rhythm of attack now
Only wearing correct belt color for grading now now
Bowing without kumite at all in dojo now today
questions.explanation: Maai = engagement distance, Hyoshi = rhythm/timing. Shodan kumite is not brawling. Control distance to be safe and effective, break opponent's rhythm, take initiative.

questions.q: "Karate ni sente nashi" from Niju Kun means what for Shodan conduct?
options: No first attack in karate - restraint first always now
Always attack first to win quickly in dojo now now
First attack scores double points always in WKF now
No rules in kumite at all for Shodan now today
questions.explanation: One of 20 Precepts. Karate is for character and protection, never to start violence. Shodan must embody restraint, karate as defense, not aggression.

questions.q: When do you use Shomen vs Hanmi hip position in Shodan basics?
options: Hanmi for defense evasion, Shomen for final power delivery
Shomen only for all techniques always without change
Hanmi only for kata without exception at all now
No difference between them at all really now now
questions.explanation: Hanmi = half-facing, protects center, faster. Shomen = square facing, full power delivery. Oi-zuki uses hanmi to enter, Gyaku-zuki finishes with shomen rotation for power.

questions.q: What is Enbusen rule that Shodan must follow in grading?
options: Start and end at same point with precise lines exact
Start anywhere and finish anywhere randomly now now
Only move forward without turns at all now now now
Random walking without pattern at all now now now
questions.explanation: Enbusen = performance line. Kata must start and finish at same point (except Tekki). Shows control of balance, turns, spatial awareness. Shodan must keep exact embusen.

questions.q: As Shodan, when you teach kohai, what does correcting Oss and Rei first teach?
options: Technique less important than spirit, respect, perseverance
Shouting is all that matters for grading now now
Belts are bought not earned in dojo now today now
Bowing is optional for Shodan kohai now today now
questions.explanation: Oss = perseverance, Rei = respect. Shodan role is not to teach fancy kicks first, but to model spirit. Correct attitude before technique.

questions.q: Why is the style called "Shotokan"?
options: Shoto was Funakoshi's pen name and Kan means hall - Shoto's hall
After a mountain in Japan called Shotokan mountain now
After a weapon type called Shoto used in Okinawa
After a tournament name called Shotokan Cup event now
questions.explanation: Shoto = waving pines, Funakoshi's poetry pen name. His students wrote Shotokan above his dojo entrance - Hall of Shoto. Name stuck as style.

questions.q: Shodan literally means:
options: First step / beginning grade - not expert level yet now
Master who knows everything in karate now today now
Final grade of karate and end of learning now today
Only tournament champion with trophy now today now
questions.explanation: Sho = beginning, Dan = grade/step. Shodan = first step, beginning. Not mastery. It means you have learned basics enough to now really start learning karate-do.

questions.q: What does achieving Shodan (1st Dan) truly mean?
options: Beginning of serious study - fundamentals mastered, journey starts
Retirement from training after getting black belt now
You now know everything in karate completely now
Time to stop learning basics forever now today
questions.explanation: Sho = first. Shodan is start of real depth: same basics, higher standard, deeper responsibility. Beginning, not end.

questions.q: On grading day, the examiner's first responsibility is:
options: Entertain parents with jokes and stories during test
Pass everyone the same regardless of standard now
Finish grading as quickly as possible to save time
Check syllabus coverage, time-in-grade and safety first
questions.explanation: Orderly, fair, safe gradings are dojo management at its most visible. Check time-in-grade, syllabus, safety, then score. Integrity before convenience.

questions.q: Traditionally, the brown belt symbolizes:
options: A maturing tree - technique hardening near black belt level
Failure to achieve black belt in time now today
A beginner who just started karate training now
A referee who only judges tournaments now today
questions.explanation: Brown means ripening: skills solidify, ego softens, student prepares to carry dojo responsibility. Like tree bark hardening.

questions.q: What is expected of a 3rd Brown in the dojo as leader?
options: Arrive late and leave early without helping anyone
Train only for themselves without helping kohai now
Avoid beginners and only train with black belts now
Lead warm-ups, assist teaching and model Dojo Kun daily
questions.explanation: Senior kyu grades are backbone of dojo: management support, teaching help and visible discipline. Sempai models rei, effort, zanshin daily.

questions.q: For Shodan prep, the phrase 'Onko Chishin' means:
options: Learning from past to guide future generations well
Copying others without understanding at all now
Forgetting tradition and doing your own thing now
Winning at all costs in tournaments always now
questions.explanation: Onko Chishin = study old to understand new. Honouring elders' path. Shodan studies history and tradition to carry karate forward faithfully.

questions.q: What is Sanbon Zuki in Zenkutsu Dachi?
options: Three Gyaku-zuki in place without moving now today
One punch then two blocks in Zenkutsu now today
Chudan, Jodan, Chudan - level change sequence
Three Jodan punches only without level change now
questions.explanation: Sanbon Zuki teaches level change and distance: chudan oi-zuki, jodan oi-zuki, then chudan gyaku-zuki with full hip rotation and kime.

questions.q: Which Heian introduces Kokutsu Dachi first?
options: Heian Shodan with only zenkutsu dachi stance now
Heian Nidan with first kokutsu dachi introduction
Heian Godan with jump and kiai now today today
Heian Sandan with spinning embusen changes now now
questions.explanation: Heian Nidan is first to introduce Kokutsu Dachi, plus Yoko Geri Keage and Shuto Uke. Heian Shodan is only Zenkutsu. Correction: Actually Heian Nidan introduces Kokutsu. Note: Some schools say Shodan has kokutsu, but standard JKA - Nidan first.

questions.q: What does Shotokan mean?
options: House of hard waves crashing loudly now today
Way of empty hand without weapons at all now
Pine forest with trees waving in wind only now
House of Shoto - Funakoshi's pen name hall
questions.explanation: Shoto = waving pines, Funakoshi's poetry pen name. Kan = house/hall. Students put Shotokan sign over his dojo entrance. Hall of Shoto.

questions.q: What does OSU mean in dojo?
options: Means hello only as casual greeting now today
Means black belt coming soon to grading now now
Means I want to fight right now today always now
To persevere under pressure with patience now
questions.explanation: From Oshi Shinobu - to endure, to push, to never give up. Embodies respect

questions.q: Why does a dojo keep accurate attendance and grading records?
options: To verify time-in-grade and keep grading fair and transparent
To sell student data to marketing companies now today
For decoration on wall without any real purpose now
Only for tournaments and never for grading purposes
questions.explanation: Good management protects belt integrity - attendance, time-in-grade and syllabus checks must be documented. Fairness and transparency.

questions.q: What is challenge of Heian Godan for Ni-Kyu?
options: Only punches inside without kicks at all now today
Slow movements only without power at all now today
First jump and combo of Heian 1-4 combined together
Ground fighting only without standing at all now today
questions.explanation: Godan contains first jump (kosa tobi), mikazuki geri, and combines all previous Heian lessons in one embusen. Required for Ni-kyu. Tests previous.

questions.q: What is Tai Sabaki with Ren Zuki?
options: Moving arms only without body movement at all now
Standing still position without shifting at all now now
Jumping backwards always without forward movement now
Body shift off line while punching with angle now
questions.explanation: At Ni-kyu, not just block-punch but whole body moves off attack line. Tai = body, Sabaki = shifting. Makes Ren Zuki effective with angle and evasion.

questions.q: Who were Funakoshi's 3 main teachers who shaped Shotokan?
options: Azato, Itosu, Matsumura who taught Shuri-te system
Bruce Lee, Ip Man, Tyson who taught modern fighting
Kano, Ueshiba, Oyama who taught other martial arts
Miyagi, Mabuni, Motobu who taught different styles
questions.explanation: Anko Azato taught strategy and philosophy, Anko Itosu created Heian kata for education, Sokon Matsumura taught Shuri-te basics. Shaped Shotokan foundation.

questions.q: What does Jinkaku Kansei ni Tsutomuru Koto mean?
options: Always win at all cost without character at all now
Seek perfection of character as primary goal always
Only strength matters without character at all now
Avoid school training and focus on fighting only now
questions.explanation: First Dojo Kun precept: character perfection is primary goal. Power without good character is dangerous approaching black belt. Character first.

questions.q: What makes Gyaku Mawashi Geri correct and safe?
options: Same as Mae Geri kick without difference at all now
No pivot needed at all for kicking high now today
Punch with foot action without hip at all now today
Opposite chamber, full hip turn, support foot pivot
questions.explanation: Requires knee chamber to opposite side, full hip turnover, 180-degree pivot of support foot, striking with heel or ball, rechamber fast.

questions.q: What is Mokuso for at Ni-Kyu level?
options: Sleeping time in dojo during class time now today
Push ups and fitness exercise for strength now now
Shouting and kiai to warm up lungs now today now
Silent meditation to clear mind and set intention
questions.explanation: Moku = silent, So = thought. Moment of silence before to leave ego outside and set intention, after to reflect and calm. Core Shotokan tradition.

questions.q: Which Sentei kata starts at 2nd Brown level?
options: Unsu advanced kata for Nidan level only now today
Gojushiho Dai advanced kata for Sandan now today
Tekki Shodan - iron horse close combat kata now
Kanku Dai only for Shodan level now today today
questions.explanation: Tekki Shodan (formerly Naihanchi) is first brown belt kata outside Heian. Teaches Kiba Dachi strength and close-distance fighting, side-to-side embusen.

questions.q: What is correct Shuto Uke in Kokutsu Dachi?
options: 50-50 weight split evenly on both legs now today
Leaning forward stance with weight front now today now
No stance needed ever for Shuto Uke now today now
70% back, thumb tucked, elbow 90 degrees exact
questions.explanation: Requires 70% weight back, front knee over foot, back leg straight, hips 45 deg, knife hand thumb tucked, elbow 90 degrees, zanshin.

questions.q: What is Kihon Ippon Kumite?
options: Free for all fighting without rules now today now
One attack announced, one block and counter now done
No blocking allowed at all in kumite now today now
Only kicking allowed without punching now today now
questions.explanation: One-step basic sparring: attacker announces attack (jodan, chudan), one attack only, defender blocks and counters with kime. Teaches Maai and timing.

questions.q: What does Karate ni Sente Nashi mean for Ni-Kyu?
options: Always attack first fast to win in kumite now today
Sente means student rank in dojo now today today now
No meaning at all in karate philosophy now today now
No first attack, defend peace with restraint always
questions.explanation: Second Niju Kun: true karateka never initiates violence physically or verbally. Moral code of non-aggression and self-control. Character over aggression.

questions.q: What is Ura Zuki (close punch) used for at Ni-Kyu?
options: Long range punch like Oi-Zuki always now today now
Close range punch with palm up under opponent chin
High kick to head level only now today now today
Bowing without technique at all now today now now
questions.explanation: Ura = reverse/inverted. Ura Zuki = close uppercut with palm up, elbow tight, under chin or solar plexus. Used

questions.q: Bassai Dai translates to what?
options: To storm a fortress - breaking through defense
Peaceful mind and calm meditation state now
Iron horse standing firm and rooted now today
Flying swallow moving lightly and swiftly now
questions.explanation: Bassai = to extract from fortress. Explosive entry, change of momentum, breaking strong defense with power switch.

questions.q: Jiyu Kumite vs Jiyu Ippon Kumite difference?
options: Free vs one attack semi-free with reaction now
Same with no difference at all between them now
No difference between them at all now today now
Point vs knockdown only difference now today now
questions.explanation: Jiyu Ippon = semi-free one attack, attacker can time attack freely, defender reacts. Jiyu Kumite = completely free sparring. Progressive steps to Shodan.

questions.q: Why is Bassai Dai key for Ik-kyu grading?
options: Easiest kata in list for beginners now today now
Only for kids grading and not for adults now now
No significance today for Shodan level now today
Storm fortress, explosive power, hip switching
questions.explanation: Bassai Dai means to storm a fortress. Teaches explosive power change, hip switching, and breaking defense with spirit and kime.

questions.q: What is Chinkuchi or Kime at Ik-kyu level?
options: Loose technique always without focus at all now
Keep muscle tight always without relaxing now now
Shout loud only without body focus now today now
Total focus at impact then relax immediately now
questions.explanation: Instant total muscle contraction, breath, hip vibration and mental focus at impact for microsecond, then immediate relaxation for shock power and speed.

questions.q: What organization did Funakoshi students create in 1949?

dictionary.definition: The bow of respect — made entering and leaving the dojo, to your sensei and to your partner. Respect made physical.
The dojo's all-purpose word: perseverance, endurance and respect in one. From Oshi Shinobu — to push and to endure.
'Place of the way'. The training hall, treated with the respect of a sacred space — shoes off, bow on entering.
'One who has gone before'. The teacher who guides the path — not just technique, but character.
The senior student. Models etiquette, mentors juniors, keeps the tradition chain alive.
The junior student. Observes, learns and honours the sempai-kohai relationship.
The kneeling bow, performed in seiza at the formal opening and closing of class.
The standing bow — used when stepping onto the training area or greeting.
The command for silent meditation at the start and end of class — calming the mind, leaving the world at the door.
'Ready'. Set your stance and your mind before the technique begins.
'Begin'. Starts the drill or the match.
'Stop'. Immediate halt — everything freezes on the word.
'Turn around'. The about-face command between drills.
'Return'. Come back to the ready position and relax.
'Attention'. Feet together, eyes forward, mind alert.
'At ease / rest'. Relax from attention.
The fundamentals — basic techniques repeated until they cannot fail under pressure.
Form — a choreographed fight against imaginary opponents, carrying the art's strategy and history.
Sparring — progressing from pre-arranged Ippon and Sanbon to free Jiyu kumite.
Analysis — unlocking the striking, grappling and throwing applications hidden inside kata movements.
'Remaining mind'. Sustained awareness after the technique ends — you never drop your guard.
Decisive focus — total commitment of power and will at the moment of impact.
Combative distance — the space between safety and the strike. Reading it wins fights.
The floor pattern a kata traces — its line of movement through the hall.
The spirit shout — unites breath, body and intent. Not noise: commitment.
Technique. Waza-ari is 'half a point' — a technique almost good enough to score full.
'Mind without ego'. The clear, spontaneous mind that acts without hesitation under pressure.
'There is no first attack in karate.' Funakoshi's precept: karate exists for protection and character, never aggression.
The stages of mastery: obey the form (Shu), break the form (Ha), transcend the form (Ri).
The five training precepts recited at the end of class — perfection of character, faithfulness, endeavour, respect, restraint.
'The way of the warrior' — the ethical code: rectitude, courage, benevolence, respect, honesty, honour, loyalty.
'Everyday mind' — the calm, present state carried from the dojo floor into daily life.
Front stance — long, 60% weight forward, front knee bent. The power stance for Oi-Zuki.
Back stance — 70% weight on the back leg. Built for defence and counter-attack.
Horse-riding stance — strong side-to-side base. The legs of Tekki.
Informal attention stance, heels together and feet turned out — the stance of bowing.
Lunge punch — stepping punch delivered with the same-side arm and leg driving forward.
Reverse punch — hip-rotated punch from the rear hand. The karate power line: floor, legs, hips, fist.
Front kick — ball of the foot, snapping upward thrust through the target.
Roundhouse kick — hip-driven circular kick striking with the instep or ball of the foot.
Side kick — in two flavours: keage (rising snap) and kekomi (driving thrust).
Rising block — forearm sweep upward against head-level attacks.
Outside-in block — forearm crossing from outside toward the centre line.
Inside-out block — the fundamental middle-level deflecting block.
Downward sweeping block — the first block most karateka ever learn.
Knife-hand block — the open-hand signature of kata like Heian Shodan.
The pulling hand — the retracting fist that anchors balance and loads hip power into every punch.
Elbow strike — the shortest, hardest close-range weapon in the arsenal.
Upper level — head and neck. Every technique names its level: Jodan, Chudan or Gedan.
Middle level — chest to stomach. The default target of Gyaku-Zuki.
Lower level — below the belt. Gedan-Barai sweeps this line clear.
Student rank below black belt, counted downward: 9th Kyu is a beginner, 1st Kyu is the last step.
Black-belt grade, counted upward: Shodan (1st) to Judan (10th).
'First step' — 1st Dan. Not the summit: the beginning of serious study.
A black-belt holder — one who has entered the dan grades.
10th Dan — a lifetime rank given for contribution to the art, far beyond technique.
1–5: Ichi, Ni, San, Shi (dojo counting), Go.
6–10: Roku, Shichi (or Nana), Hachi, Kyu, Ju.
The state of remaining awareness after technique, mind stays alert.
Focus of power - total concentration at impact.
Five guiding principles of Shotokan dojo.
The belt that holds the gi and shows rank. Its knot shows etiquette — tied over the spirit, not fashion.
The training uniform — correctly called Karate-Gi. White means beginner mind. Keep it clean, folded, respected.
The top side of the dojo — where the shomen shrine or sensei's picture sits. Students sit facing kamiza during mokuso.
The front of the dojo. Where respect is shown with ritsu-rei on entry and exit.
Proper etiquette of bowing — when, how deep, how long. Reigi is the heart of dojo behavior.
Proper manners and procedural etiquette inside the dojo — how to sit, bow, receive correction.
Formal kneeling posture — knees folded, back straight. Used for zarei and mokuso.
Cross-legged sitting allowed when seiza is painful. Still keeps back straight and respectful.
Line-up command — students form ranks facing kamiza for start or end of class.
Turn command — about-face, usually followed by yoi.
Body shifting — moving the body off the attack line to create angle. Footwork is defence.
Entering directly into the opponent's space — the boldest form of tai sabaki.
Body shifting by stepping back and rotating — yielding to create counter-attack.
Viewing the distant mountain — seeing the opponent whole, not staring at one part. Peripheral, calm vision.
Initiative — the timing of attack. Go no Sen, Sen no Sen, Sen Sen no Sen.
Late initiative — defending after the opponent attacks, then countering. The beginner's timing.
Simultaneous initiative — attacking at the instant opponent decides to attack. Stealing the moment.
Pre-emptive initiative — sensing intent before movement and acting first. Highest timing.
Meeting at the start — intercepting the attack at its inception. Deai is sen no sen in motion.
Stopping just short — control that halts one inch from target. Proof of mastery, not weakness.
Combined or added points — referee call when two techniques score together.
Decision — judges call for a decision in a tied match.
A draw — no winner decided. Common in enbu or team kata when scores equal.
Half-point in competition — a technique almost perfect, one point short of ippon.
Full point — a decisive technique with good form, timing, distance, and zanshin.
15 seconds left — timekeeper's warning that the bout is ending. Final chance to score.
Immovable stance — like zenkutsu but feet in line, rooted and unshakeable. Stance of Sochin.
Closed feet stance — feet together, knees together. Formal attention stance.
Natural open-leg stance — feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out. Ready stance before yoi.
Cat stance — 90% weight on rear leg, front foot light like a cat's paw. For quick kicks and sweeps.
Hourglass stance — toes in, knees in, rooted. Breathing stance of Goju and Uechi.
Half-moon stance — like sanchin but wider, knees bent outward. Stance of Hangetsu kata.
Crossed-leg stance — rear knee behind front, weight low. Often a transition in kata.
L-shaped stance — feet form the Japanese character for L. Narrow, deceptive distance.
Inverted punch — palm up, short uppercut aimed at chin or solar plexus in close range.
Vertical punch — fist vertical, like holding a hammer. Used in close quarters.
Jab punch — lead hand snap with no hip switch. Fast, probing.
Double punch — both fists punch together. Strength of two hands in one line.
Mountain punch — one arm jodan, one chudan simultaneously. U-shape of a mountain.
Combined punch — both fists to same level, usually chudan double.
Spear hand — fingertips thrusting as a blade. Requires conditioned fingers.
Knife-hand strike — outer edge of hand slashing to neck or temple. Not a block.
Ridge-hand — thumb side of hand striking, opposite of shuto.
Palm-heel strike — heel of palm driving upward to chin or chest.
Back-fist strike — snapping back of fist to temple or nose.
Hammer fist — bottom of fist swinging down like a hammer.
Bent-wrist strike — striking with bent wrist, pushing down.
Crescent kick — foot arcs inside or outside, sole slaps away opponent's hand.
Back kick — thrusting heel backward, looking over shoulder. Strongest kick.
Spinning back roundhouse — full turn with heel. High-risk, high-reward.
Jumping front kick — both knees lift, then front kick in air.
Double jumping kick — one foot then other in same jump. Footwork of Kanku-Dai.
Heel drop — stomping heel down onto thigh, foot, or face.
Knee strike — rising knee to body or face in close range.
X-block — forearms crossed to block jodan or gedan. Juji means cross.
Augmented block — one forearm supports the other. Double strength.
Scooping block — palm scoops under opponent's kick to lift and unbalance.
Flowing block — palm sweeping aside attack like water.
Hooking block — wrist hooking and pulling opponent's arm.
Back-hand block — using back of hand to deflect.
Palm-heel block — palm heel pressing outward to stop punch.
Dropping block — forearm dropping down to block low kick or leg.
Foot sweep — sweeping opponent's foot to break balance. Tai sabaki's partner.
Consecutive kicks — same leg kicking twice before landing.
Consecutive kicks in sequence — often mae-geri then mawashi-geri without setting foot down.
Rotating palms kata — breathing and soft circular hands. Goju's other half to Sanchin.
Three battles — mind, body, spirit. Kata and breathing exercise teaching rooted tension.
Hard breathing — powerful, audible exhale with tension. Sanchin's breath.
Soft breathing — silent, hidden exhale for recovery and calm. Breath of Hangetsu.
Okinawan term for total body connection — wrist snap that ties floor to fist in one instant.
Sticky, heavy hands — weighted feeling in arms from correct breathing and relaxation.
Core power — the hip and lower abdomen's linked twist that powers every technique.
Lower abdomen center — the body's power center, two inches below navel. Where breath gathers.
Belly or gut — seat of courage and spirit. Strong hara means unshakable.
Center line — imaginary line down your middle and opponent's. Control it, you control the fight.
Entering line — stepping into opponent's attack to cut it short.
Head — including atama-uchi, head strike, rarely used.
Throat — vital point. Shuto or nukite to nodo is decisive.
Groin — kinteki-geri is prohibited in dojo kumite but studied for self-defense.
Joint — kansetsu-geri attacks knee joint. Banned in sport, real in bunkai.
Foot blade — outer edge of foot used in yoko-geri kekomi.
Ball of foot — striking surface for mae-geri and mawashi-geri.
Heel — striking surface for ushiro-geri and kakato-geri.
Wrist — where kime locks. Strong tekubi means strong punch.
Forearm — ude-uke means forearm block. Forearms conditioned in kote-kitae.
Shoulder wheel — lifting throw where opponent rides your shoulders, hidden in kata bunkai.
Circle throw — foot on opponent's stomach, rolling back to throw. Seen in Enpi bunkai.
Maximum efficiency, minimum effort — Jigoro Kano's principle that karate also follows.
Mutual welfare and benefit — growing together with partner, not defeating partner.
Straw mat flooring — in modern dojo replaced by mats, but bow still honors the space.
